target_pattern: Use estar + adjective to express temporary states, emotions, health, and current food condition; maintain adjective gender/number agreement and contrast with ser when needed.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Treating to be as one universal verb and ignoring agreement.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: Use estar for current condition/state and adjust adjective endings to match who or what is being described.
natural_examples: Estoy cansado porque tengo que trabajar.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each in Spanish using estar correctly and matching adjective agreement. No answer key until the end.
prompts_en: I am sad because I have to work.
I am happy because I can rest.
We are tired because we cannot sleep.

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Estoy cansado. -> change to feminine speaker.
Base: María está enferma. -> turn into question.
Base: Ellos están nerviosos. -> change to feminine plural.
Base: Estoy triste porque tengo que trabajar. -> change reason to no puedo dormir.
Base: El café está caliente. -> make it negative.
Base: La cerveza está fría. -> change to plural subject las cervezas.
Base: ¿Cómo estás? -> answer with confundido (male speaker).
Base: Los tacos están deliciosos. -> change to singular el taco.
Base: Nosotros estamos preocupados. -> change to nosotras.
Base: ¿Por qué estás triste? -> answer with porque no puedo hablar con mi amiga.
Base: La fruta está fría. -> change to las frutas.
Base: Juan está contento. -> make it negative.
Base: Estoy feliz. -> add reason with porque voy a descansar.
Base: Las mujeres están cansadas. -> change to masculine plural los hombres.

contrastive_discrimination.instructions: Choose the best option and write in Spanish.
prompts: I am tired (right now). (estoy vs soy)
I am a patient person. (soy vs estoy)
María is sick today. (está enferma vs es enferma)
The tacos are delicious. (están deliciosos vs son deliciosos) in current tasting context.
How are you? (¿cómo estás? vs ¿cómo eres?)
What are you like? (¿cómo eres? vs ¿cómo estás?)
The coffee is hot. (está caliente vs es caliente) as current serving condition.
They are worried because they have a test. (están preocupados vs son preocupados)
I am happy today. (estoy feliz vs soy feliz) temporary emphasis.
The beer is cold. (está fría vs es fría) in drinking context.

guided_personal_writing.instructions: Write one Spanish sentence for each specific meaning.
prompts: You are tired because you slept badly.
You are happy because you are going to travel.
You are worried about work today.
You are nervous before an important meeting.
Your friend is sick and cannot go out.
Your coworkers are stressed this week.
The coffee is too hot right now.
The food is delicious tonight.
The drink is cold and refreshing.
You are confused and need help.
You are not sad anymore.
Your family is content today.
You are angry because you have too many tasks.
You are calm now, not nervous.
You are happy because you can rest tomorrow.

prompts_en: I am not feeling great today.
The food is really good today.
I cannot think clearly right now.
She is in a bad mood.
The coffee is too cold now.

common_errors.why_it_happens: English uses one to be verb.
Trait vs temporary condition is mixed.

common_errors.mistake: soy bien for I am good

common_errors.why_it_happens: Sentence linking in Spanish is underused.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Estoy triste porque no puedo dormir.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Cross-pattern confusion with modal + infinitive lessons.
enojado and enfadado mixed without awareness.
common_errors.correct_spanish: Both are valid; use one consistently in context.

Estamos cansados porque no podemos dormir.
